extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and members of the public petitioning the USPTO (OPLA) regarding public use/on-sale issues and submitting trade secret/proprietary materials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive standards for filing, processing, and adjudicating petitions under 37 CFR 1.292 (public use/on-sale) and for submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials to the USPTO. Covers formal requirements, examiner prima facie determinations, hearings, testimony, final decisions, and confidential-material submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for petition under 37 CFR 1.292
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be submitted prior to the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under § 1.311, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a practical matter, submit as soon as possible after becoming aware of the application to ensure consideration. Petitions filed after publication or mailing of a notice of allowance will be dismissed as untimely. A petition submitted prior to those dates but not provided to OPLA with the application before issuance/abandonment may be entered but dismissed as moot. Petitions submitted after final rejection may be considered if application is still pending and unpublished; prosecution will not ordinarily be reopened if the alleged public use/sale is merely cumulative of prior art cited in the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a public use petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public other than the applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.292; an attorney or other representative may file on behalf of an unnamed principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes private persons, corporations, and government agencies. A party to an interference generally may not file a petition as to an application involved in the interference (public use/on-sale issues in an interference must be raised by motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(1)), except certain exceptions for interferences declared prior to Feb 11, 1985 are noted. Petitions filed on/after Feb 11, 1985 are not allowed if arising from an interference declared on/after that date unless the interference arose from one declared prior to that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required formal contents of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be in writing, specifically identify the application (by application number or serial number and filing date), and should include a listing of all affidavits/declarations and exhibits relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale', including necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts, to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the alleged public use/on-sale subject matter. The petition and accompanying papers must either (A) reflect that a copy has been served on the applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent, or (B) be filed in duplicate if service is not possible. Recommended identifying information (if known) to place on the petition includes: name of applicant(s); application number; confirmation number; filing date; title of invention; Technology Center art unit number; name of examiner; current status and location of application; and 'ATTENTION:' followed by the Office area to which the petition is directed. Petition should be clearly identified as 'PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(j), and must be served on the applicant in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248 or filed in duplicate if service is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy served on applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent should be a complete copy including all photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, flowcharts, or other documents relied on. The petition filed in the Office should reflect service by an appropriate 'Certificate of Service.' Duplicate copies should be submitted only when, after diligent effort, service was not possible. All subsequent papers must be served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA preliminary handling and formal review
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) for formal requirement review and to ascertain whether the petition warrants consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA will review whether the petition was filed prior to publication/notice of allowance, whether the alleged use/sale occurred in this country more than one year before the effective filing date, whether affidavits/declarations and exhibits are provided, whether papers were filed in duplicate or served, and whether required fees have been paid. OPLA will order the application file and ascertain status so appropriate action may be taken. If service was not indicated and no duplicate filed, OPLA may contact applicant/attorney to determine if service occurred and may request a duplicate before referring to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for petitions by parties to an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for institution of public use proceedings shall not be filed by a party to an interference as to an application involved in the interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public use and on-sale issues in an interference must be raised by motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(1). There are narrow historical exceptions related to interferences declared prior to Feb 11, 1985; petitioners once involved in a terminated interference are treated as ex parte petitioners and lose access to application contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination of prima facie case
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner determines whether the facts asserted in the affidavits/declarations and supported by exhibits establish a prima facie case that public use or sale in this country more than one year before the effective filing date would result in a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make this determination the examiner must identify exactly what was in public use or on sale, whether it occurred in this country more than one year before the effective filing date, and whether the pending claims 'read' on or are obvious over what has been shown to be in public use or on sale. The examiner should compare all pending claims with the matter alleged to have been in use or on sale, not just claims identified by petitioner. If the examiner finds a prima facie case, he/she forwards a memorandum to the OPLA staff member summarizing alleged facts, comparing at least one claim with the alleged device, and other pertinent facts to aid the preliminary hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements when petition alleges obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition alleges that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information relied on and explain how the prior art or other information, in combination with the subject matter alleged to be in public use/on sale, renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not expected to perform a prior art search in evaluating the petition. However, if the examiner is aware of prior art or other information which, in the examiner's opinion, renders the claims obvious over the subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the examiner may determine that a prima facie case is made out even if the petition only alleged anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner concludes a prima facie case has been established, the Director may hold a preliminary hearing; parties will be notified of the examiner’s conclusion and the time/date of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte cases no copy of the examiner’s memorandum will be forwarded to the petitioner; notification of the hearing is essentially an order to show cause why a public use proceeding should not be held. No new evidence is to be introduced or discussed at the preliminary hearing. The OPLA staff member establishes the hearing format; the examiner may attend only as an observer. Where the examiner concludes no prima facie showing, parties are notified and application proceedings resume without opportunity to be heard on that decision. In ex parte hearings great care must be taken to avoid discussing matters of the application file not already known to petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony requirements and limits in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory bar can only be established by testimony taken in accordance with normal rules of evidence, including cross-examination; affidavits/declarations/exhibits accompanying the petition are not testimony and cannot be used as petitioner’s evidence unless submitted as part of petitioner’s testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for taking testimony is similar to interference testimony. Examiner will set a schedule for testimony and filing of record and briefs (detailed schedule template provided). A certified transcript of a deposition must be filed within one month after the deposition date (37 CFR 41.157). Testimony is limited to issues of public use or on sale; no testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale. Parties may agree to a different schedule provided the last brief is filed no later than the specified final date; extensions are limited under 37 CFR 1.136 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision format and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s final decision should analyze the testimony and state conclusions, analogous to a Board decision in an interference; the examiner is not bound by the prior prima facie finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes a public use or sale bar exists, enter a rejection predicated on the evidence and findings from the public use proceeding. Even if no rejection is made, the examiner’s written action should reflect that 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity was considered. If the examiner concludes a prima facie case was not established or has been rebutted, the written action should so indicate. Use of reasons for allowance under 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate. No review is available from the examiner’s final decision in the public use proceedings except via a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting supervisory vacation for a showing of clear error; appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141-145 is available once the application returns to ex parte status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and public availability of petitions/papers in application file
rubrics_metrics.description: When public use petitions and accompanying papers are submitted they, or a notice in lieu thereof, will be entered in the application file if the petition meets requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitions/papers are too bulky they may be entered as a notice in lieu of the petition; any public use papers not physically entered will be publicly available whenever the application file wrapper is available. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual section 3.3 and 3.4. If petition not submitted prior to publication/notice of allowance it should not be entered; applicant should be notified the petition is untimely and not being entered. Specific handling rules apply for untimely petitions regarding discarding originals/duplicates and sending originals to applicant with notification of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction/nonelected claim handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition alleges that subject matter covering both elected and nonelected claims is a statutory bar, only that part of the petition drawn to the subject matter of the elected claims will be considered initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public use proceeding is instituted it may not be limited to elected subject matter and may include nonelected subject matter. Any evidence adduced on the nonelected subject matter may be used in any subsequently-filed application claiming that subject matter without requirement of a new fee (37 CFR 1.17(j)). The petitioner will not be heard regarding the appropriateness of any restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special timing and handling for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.176).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition cannot be filed within the 2-month period, petitioner may submit later but must be aware reissue applications are 'special' and later petitions may be received after examiner action. A request for extension of the 2-month period must be filed as a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f), must explain why additional time is necessary and the nature of allegations, and must be served on applicant. OPLA will critically review extension requests and grant only as necessary for minimal period. 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions should be marked prominently (and hand-carried if urgent); petitioners may seek waiver of the 2-month delay under 37 CFR 1.183 when accompanied by the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling untimely petitions and disposition of originals/duplicates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is not submitted prior to the earliest of publication or mailing of a notice of allowance it should not be entered in the application file and applicant should be notified that the petition is untimely and is not being entered in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling varies by whether service was indicated: (A) Where the petition includes an indication of service of copy on applicant, the original petition should be discarded. (B) Where the petition does not include an indication of service and a duplicate copy is or is not present, the duplicate copy (if present) should be discarded and the original petition should be sent to the applicant along with the notification of nonentry. OPLA may reproduce petitions in limited circumstances rather than delay referral to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information regardless of confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors and others covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c) and 1.555 have a duty to disclose to the Office information they are aware of which is material to patentability, regardless of its classification as trade secret, proprietary, or subject to protective order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.56(b) defines information as material to patentability when it is not cumulative and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination with other information, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting patentability. A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under a preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each claim term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, before considering contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials considered trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order must be clearly labeled and filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container, accompanied by a transmittal letter and (recommended) a petition under 37 CFR 1.59 to expunge if not material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each document/item must be labeled as 'Trade Secret', 'Proprietary', or 'Subject To Protective Order' (avoid labels 'Confidential', 'Secret', 'Restricted' or 'Restricted Data' to prevent confusion with national security markings). If 'Subject to Protective Order', list the proceeding/tribunal on each document. The envelope/container must include complete identifying information for the file (application no., filing date, title, TC art unit, examiner). Examples of envelope labels and form fields are provided. The transmittal letter must state materials are considered trade secrets/proprietary/subject to protective order and are submitted under MPEP § 724. A petition under 37 CFR 1.59 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) to expunge non-material information should accompany the envelope/container. To avoid mishandling, hand-carry to the Customer Window is recommended; mailing address and hand-carry location provided. Upon receipt, the Office places the envelope in an Artifact folder for IFW applications or retains the envelope with sealed contents for paper applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible submission with deletions to avoid disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In some circumstances, information may be submitted with appropriate deletions of nonmaterial portions so that legitimate trade secrets/proprietary material will not be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletions should be done only where there will be no loss of information material to patentability under 37 CFR 1.56 or 1.555.
